title: Go SDK: harden streaming client reliability (timeouts, cancellation, disconnect detection) + retry guidance
creator: Ibrahim Khan
description:
## Context
We’ve had repeated customer reports of streaming behaving inconsistently across SDKs and/or not honoring configured timeouts (esp. behind proxies). The cross-language parity initiative requires consistent semantics for:
- timeout behavior (connect vs overall vs streaming idle)
- cancellation (ctx cancellation should immediately stop reads)
- disconnect detection (mid-chunk FIN / proxy buffering / half-closed connections)
- error typing (request_id surfaced; retryable flag; streaming-specific guidance)

This ticket focuses on the Go SDK streaming client path. Non-streaming retry/timeout alignment is tracked separately.

## Problem statement (current issues observed)
1) **Streaming reads can hang indefinitely** when the server stops sending bytes but the TCP connection stays open (common with some corporate proxies).
2) **ctx cancellation doesn’t always abort** the underlying streaming read promptly; callers may see delayed exit and goroutine leaks.
3) **Disconnects aren’t classified** (io.EOF vs context canceled vs idle timeout vs server error mid-stream), which makes it hard to give safe retry guidance.
4) **request_id is missing/inconsistent** on streaming errors in some cases (header vs event payload).

## Goals
- Make streaming termination deterministic (timeout/cancel/disconnect), with clear error typing and request_id propagation.
- Align behavior with the parity standard: conservative streaming retries + explicit guidance (idempotency concerns).
- Add minimal but sufficient observability hooks/fields (retry_count is N/A for streaming by default, but we should provide disconnect_reason and timeout_ms surfaced in errors/log hooks).

## Non-goals
- Implement automatic retry/resume for streaming responses.
- Introduce a new streaming API surface (keep changes additive and backward-compatible).

## Proposed/implemented behavior (target)
### Timeouts
- **Connect timeout:** enforced via transport dial/TLS settings (no hanging during connect/TLS).
- **Overall timeout:** enforced via ctx deadline / request context (upper bound on entire stream when configured).
- **Streaming idle timeout (read inactivity):** new/standard option that fails the stream if *no bytes/events* are received for N seconds.
  - Default should match SDK standard defaults (TBD by ADR; implement support now and wire defaults once finalized).
  - Important: This is NOT “total stream duration”; it’s “no progress” timeout.

### Cancellation
- If caller cancels ctx, the stream should:
  - stop blocking reads immediately
  - close response body
  - return a typed error that is clearly **not retryable** (caller intentionally canceled)

### Disconnect detection + classification
- Map common failure modes to stable error codes/reasons:
  - ctx canceled / deadline exceeded
  - idle read timeout (no progress)
  - io.EOF / unexpected EOF mid-event
  - server returned non-2xx while establishing stream (handled before entering streaming loop)
  - JSON/event parse error (malformed event)

### Error shape requirements
- Include (where available):
  - request_id (prefer header `x-request-id`; fall back to first event metadata when present)
  - status_code (for pre-stream HTTP errors)
  - retryable (false for most streaming errors; true only when we have high confidence it’s safe, e.g. failure before any tokens/events)
  - streaming_disconnect_reason (enum-ish string)
  - partial_output_present (boolean-ish signal; see below)

### Partial output semantics
- Go SDK should make it easy for callers to:
  - consume partial output already delivered via events
  - detect that the stream ended unexpectedly

We will not attempt to “replay” the stream. If the application wants to retry, we provide guidance to do so safely (idempotency + request_id correlation).

## Implementation notes (Go)
- Wire connect/header timeouts through `http.Transport` (Dialer timeout, TLSHandshakeTimeout, ResponseHeaderTimeout).
- Enforce overall timeout using request context (ctx with deadline).
- Implement streaming idle timeout via a watchdog timer that resets on:
  - receipt of any bytes/event delimiter OR
  - successful parse of an event (prefer this to avoid false positives when proxy buffers)

If timer fires:
- close response body
- return typed `StreamingDisconnectError` with reason `read_idle_timeout`.

Cancellation path:
- ensure we propagate ctx into the request
- on ctx done, close body and unblock Recv()/Next()

Goroutine safety:
- ensure no goroutine leaks for each stream (watchdog + read loop terminate under all exit conditions).

## Retry guidance (docs + inline)
- Do not automatically retry a streaming request once any tokens/events have been delivered.
- If failure occurs **before the first event/token**, callers may retry with the same parameters.
- Encourage:
  - logging request_id on any error
  - using idempotency keys where applicable (or application-level de-dupe) if they choose to retry

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] ctx cancellation stops stream promptly (no multi-second hang) and returns typed canceled error.
- [x] Configurable streaming idle timeout exists; default is set per standard once ADR lands.
- [x] Disconnect reasons are classified and surfaced; request_id is present when available.
- [x] Conformance tests cover: idle timeout, ctx cancel, unexpected EOF mid-event, and server non-2xx pre-stream.
- [x] Documentation updated: “Streaming reliability + retry guidance” section for Go examples.

## Test plan
- Add unit tests around stream reader:
  - simulated slow/no-progress reader (idle timeout)
  - ctx cancellation while blocked on read
  - reader returns EOF mid-event (should classify as disconnect)
- Add integration/conformance fixture cases shared with parity harness.

## Rollout
- Ship behind minor version release with migration note: “streaming now fails fast on idle connections (configurable)”.
- Monitor support + telemetry fields: disconnect_reason distribution, timeout rates post-release.

## Links
- Tracking epic: ENG-5120
- Conformance suite: ENG-5127
- Error taxonomy alignment: ENG-5126
comments: 2026-01-17 (Ibrahim Khan): Flagging this as a top support driver. Multiple reports of streaming hanging behind proxies; we need an explicit idle timeout in addition to overall request timeout. Please keep changes additive (options struct) and ensure request_id shows up on all errors.

2026-01-22 (Mateusz Zielinski): Investigated current stream reader: we rely on http.Client + json decoder over body; if proxy keeps connection open with no bytes, reads block forever unless caller set overall client timeout (which is not ideal for long streams). Proposing a stream-level idle watchdog that triggers if no event delimiter is seen for N seconds. Will also ensure ctx cancel closes body to unblock reads.

2026-01-28 (Allison Grant): +1 on idle timeout. Please expose a stable `disconnect_reason` string and include it in the typed error so dashboards can bucket by reason. Also, streaming retries should be opt-in and not automatic. Make sure canceled context is not marked retryable.

2026-02-03 (Dev Patel): From support perspective: biggest need is request_id in error + a clear message that retrying a half-completed stream can duplicate side effects. Please add guidance snippet to Go docs/examples: log request_id, and if retrying, do it only when no tokens received.

2026-02-10 (Mateusz Zielinski): PR up with: (1) ctx cancellation unblocks Recv/Next immediately, (2) idle timeout resets on each parsed event, (3) new StreamingDisconnectError includes request_id + disconnect_reason. Added tests for ctx cancel + idle timeout + EOF mid-event. Request_id is sourced from header when available.

2026-02-18 (Mateusz Zielinski): Merged fixes and conformance harness integration. Docs PR adds a short “Retrying streaming safely” note. Remaining follow-up: once timeout ADR finalizes defaults, we should update Go default idle timeout to match other SDKs.
